chapter: Clubs, publishers, unions and life in Denver
title: People could dance in the 1920s and 30s; today's can't keep time
summary: Horace says dancers in the old Midwestern ballrooms like the Frog Hop in St. Joseph kept time, while young dancers today are off the beat.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Uh-huh. In the '20's and '30's, did you find that the people who came to the dances, the audiences and the dancers and so on, were they as conscious of names of tunes, you know? Were they strongly requesting things or did they pretty much just dig the style of the band and the fact that it was your band or Fletcher's band, you know, the name band?

Tom, I tell you, speaking generally from back in those days, I hate to say it but those people in those days could dance, man. They would dance by anything. Even the young kids of today. This is one thing that bothers me. I know some clubs that we play right now. I see some of these young kids get on the floor, man, and they can't keep time. They dance all out of time, and they look like they're wrestling on the floor.

It's honest -- the truth, and I feel so bad about it because right away I think, just as you asked me, back in the '20's and '30's the fathers and the mothers of these kids, they danced, man. I never will forget one time, for instance, that I played -- well, I was with Fletcher when we played this particular -- St. Joe, Missouri. We played a ballroom down there called the Frog Hop, and they did just that. They hopped. They could dance, man, and that's just one example. All through Iowa, Minnesota and all those places, in those days, man, the people danced. Of course, we played a lot of ballrooms and clubs, you know, but the people could dance. They'd keep in time.

Why, now the kids dance so bad, honest to goodness, if I was playing a solo and I was looking out at them, and they danced off beat, man, I'd quit looking at them because they'd throw me, you know, if I let them. You know, one of those things?

So it's a pathetic thing, and this type of dancing where -- I'm not criticizing, but I'm just telling you the funny things that happened, you know, which you can see from the bandstand, but a couple sometimes -- a young couple will get on the floor.
